questions.q_en: Identify the below granular structure first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade.
questions.solution_en:
• Ribosomes are the granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade (1953).

• They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane. The eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S while the prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S.

• Each ribosome has two subunits, larger and smaller subunits (as in above Figure).

• The two subunits of 80S ribosomes are 60S and 40S while that of 70S ribosomes are 50S and 30S.

• Here 'S' (Svedberg's Unit) stands for the sedimentation coefficient; it is indirectly a measure of density and size. Both 70S and 80S ribosomes are composed of two subunits.

questions.q_en: Which of the following statements is NOT part of the cell theory as understood today?
options_en: All living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells
All cells arise from pre-existing cells
Cells are the basic functional units of living organisms
Cells can arise spontaneously from non-living matter
questions.solution_en: The cell theory states that all cells arise from pre-existing cells. The idea that cells can arise spontaneously from non-living matter (abiogenesis) is not part of the modern cell theory.

questions.solution_en: Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller and multiply more rapidly than eukaryotic cells. Eukaryotic cells have membrane-bound organelles. questions.q_en: The main arena of cellular activities in both plant and animal cells is the:
questions.solution_en: The cytoplasm is the main arena of cellular activities in both plant and animal cells, where various chemical reactions occur to keep the cell in the 'living state'. The nucleus contains the genetic material, organelles perform specific functions, and the cell membrane regulates transport.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is a non-membrane bound organelle found in all cells
questions.solution_en:
Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells - both eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic. Mitochondria, the nucleus, and the endoplasmic reticulum are membrane-bound organelles.

Further insights:

Animal cells lack a cell wall. Plant cells have a cell wall made of cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins, fungal cells have a cell wall, and most bacterial cells have a cell wall (except Mycoplasma).

questions.q_en: The fluid mosaic model describes the structure of the:
questions.solution_en: The fluid mosaic model proposed by Singer and Nicolson describes the structure of the plasma membrane. It highlights the quasi-fluid nature of the lipid bilayer and the lateral movement of proteins within it.
questions.solution_hi: The fluid mosaic model proposed by Singer and Nicolson describes the structure of the plasma membrane. It highlights the quasi-fluid nature of the lipid bilayer and the lateral movement of proteins within it.

questions.q_en: The transport of molecules across the membrane against their concentration gradient that requires energy is called:
questions.solution_en: Active transport is an energy-dependent process in which ATP is utilized to transport ions or molecules across the membrane against their concentration gradient, i.e., from lower to higher concentration. Passive transport does not require energy and occurs along the concentration gradient.

Passive transport does not require energy and occurs along the concentration gradient.

questions.q_en: Which of the following organelles is NOT considered part of the endomembrane system?
questions.solution_en: The endomembrane system includes the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles because their functions are coordinated. Mitochondria, chloroplasts, and peroxisomes are not considered part of the endomembrane system as their functions are not coordinated with these components.

questions.q_en: The major site for the synthesis of lipids in animal cells is the:
questions.solution_en: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is the major site for the synthesis of lipids, including steroidal hormones in animal cells. The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is primarily involved in protein synthesis and secretion.
questions.solution_hi: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is the major site for the synthesis of lipids, including steroidal hormones in animal cells. The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is primarily involved in protein synthesis and secretion.

questions.q_en: Membrane-bound vesicular structures rich in hydrolytic enzymes, active at acidic pH, are called:
questions.solution_en: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the Golgi apparatus, rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases) optimally active at the acidic pH, capable of digesting macromolecules.
questions.solution_hi: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the Golgi apparatus, rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases) optimally active at the acidic pH, capable of digesting macromolecules.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct about the cell cycle?

I.DNA replication occurs during the S phase of interphase.

II. The M phase, or mitosis, is a very short phase, typically lasting more than 95% of the total cell cycle duration in human cells.
questions.solution_en: Statement I is correct as the S phase (Synthesis phase) is when DNA synthesis or replication takes place. Statement II is incorrect. The interphase lasts for more than 95% of the duration of the cell cycle, while the M phase (cell division proper) lasts for only about an hour in a 24-hour cycle of a human cell.
questions.solution_hi: Statement I is correct as the S phase (Synthesis phase) is when DNA synthesis or replication takes place. Statement II is incorrect. The interphase lasts for more than 95% of the duration of the cell cycle, while the M phase (cell division proper) lasts for only about an hour in a 24-hour cycle of a human cell.

questions.q_en: Plastids containing chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments responsible for trapping light energy are called:
questions.solution_en: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments which are responsible for trapping light energy essential for photosynthesis. Chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments giving yellow, orange, or red colours. Leucoplasts are colourless plastids storing nutrients.

Chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments giving yellow, orange, or red colours. Leucoplasts are colourless plastids storing nutrients.

questions.q_en: The sequence of amino acids in a protein is called its:
questions.solution_en: The sequence of amino acids, i.e., the positional information in a protein, is called the primary structure of a protein. Secondary structure refers to the folding of the polypeptide chain into helix or sheets. Tertiary structure is the overall 3-dimensional folding of the polypeptide. Quaternary structure involves the arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits.

Quaternary structure involves the arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits.

questions.q_en: Enzymes that catalyze the linking together of two compounds are classified as:
questions.solution_en: Ligases are enzymes that catalyze the linking together of 2 compounds, for example, enzymes which catalyze the joining of C-O, C-S, C-N, P-O etc. bonds. Hydrolases catalyze hydrolysis reactions, lyases catalyze removal of groups leaving double bonds, and isomerases catalyze inter-conversion of isomers.

questions.q_en: The phase of the cell cycle between two successive M phases is called:
options_hi: interphase
questions.solution_en: The interphase represents the phase between two successive M phases. The M phase is the phase of actual cell division. Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm, and karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
questions.solution_hi: The interphase represents the phase between two successive M phases. The M phase is the phase of actual cell division. Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm, and karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.

questions.q_en: During which phase of the cell cycle does DNA replication take place?
questions.solution_en: The S (synthesis) phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. The G1 phase is for growth before DNA replication, the G2 phase is for preparation for mitosis after DNA replication, and the M phase is the actual cell division phase.

questions.q_en: The process of pairing of homologous chromosomes during meiosis is called:
questions.solution_en: During the zygotene stage of prophase I in meiosis, chromosomes start pairing together, and this process of association is called synapsis. Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material, chiasmata are the X-shaped structures representing sites of crossing over, and terminalisation is the movement of chiasmata towards the ends of chromosomes.

Match the phase of mitosis with its key event:

i. Prophasea. Chromosomes align at the equator
ii. Metaphaseb. Chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and their identity is lost

iv. Telophased. Centromeres split and chromatids separate

questions.solution_en: Prophase is marked by the initiation of condensation of chromosomal material. During metaphase, chromosomes come to lie at the equator. In anaphase, centromeres split and chromatids separate. At telophase, chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and lose their identity.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct concerning enzymes?

I. Almost all enzymes are proteins, although some nucleic acids can also act as enzymes (ribozymes).

II. Enzymes work most efficiently at very high temperatures (above 60°C) and pressures.
questions.solution_en: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect. Enzymes generally function in a narrow range of temperature, with optimal activity at the optimum temperature, and high temperatures typically lead to denaturation and loss of enzymatic activity (say above 40°C).
questions.solution_hi: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect. Enzymes generally function in a narrow range of temperature, with optimal activity at the optimum temperature, and high temperatures typically lead to denaturation and loss of enzymatic activity (say above 40°C).
